sources.title: The 4 Components of Nonviolent Communication — Rosenberg framework teaching sheet
sources.inspected_sections: One-page distinctions for observation, feeling, need and request
sources.supported_use: Names the four planning distinctions used in 16.02.
sources.limits: Not an outcome study or a universal communication norm. Reasoning/boundary work and all cases are original additions; broad claims about universal needs are not adopted.

sources.title: Barrett et al. (2019), Emotional Expressions Reconsidered
sources.inspected_sections: Abstract, scope discussion and context/variability account
sources.supported_use: Facial movement does not supply a single invariant emotion label.
sources.limits: Facial research is not a validated decoder for voice, gesture or every culture. No images, action-unit training or deception detection reproduced.
sources.correction_inspected: Publisher corrigendum text inspected: Figure 5 image attribution, action-unit activation labels, improved images and acknowledgment. No affected figure or action-unit claim is used here.

sources.title: Correction to Huang et al. (2017), It does not hurt to ask (2025)
sources.kind: journal correction and original abstract reproduced by publisher through PubMed
sources.inspected_sections: Correction abstract and included original abstract
sources.supported_use: Audit reports minor reporting corrections and unchanged conclusions; original work concerns question asking and liking in studied conversations.
sources.limits: Not a retraction. No universal question quota or group-conversation benefit claimed. The independent reanalysis S04 is a distinct methodological dispute, not the same event. Full audit data were not reanalyzed.

sources.title: Kluger and Malloy (2019), Question asking as a dyadic behavior
sources.inspected_sections: Abstract describing social-relations reanalysis of Study 3
sources.supported_use: Reanalysis challenges equating second-date offers with liking and question asking with listening.
sources.limits: Only abstract inspected; PMC full-text route challenged access. Does not establish an opposite universal rule or reanalyze all original studies. Rehearsal uses no numerical question target.

sources.title: Eyal, Steffel and Epley (2018), Perspective mistaking
sources.supported_use: Separates imagined perspective taking from getting new information through conversation.
sources.limits: Author-hosted abstract inspected; linked PDF failed retrieval. Claims limited to its reported tasks and final experiment; not a guarantee of accuracy or a reason to compel disclosure.

sources.title: GSA Digital.gov — Write for the reader
sources.inspected_sections: Learn about users; focus on task needs; separate audiences
sources.supported_use: Audience needs and tasks should inform how information is organized.
sources.limits: No claim of legal compliance, universal reading level or validated effectiveness for the supplied readers. Does not authorize demographic stereotypes.

sources.title: W3C WAI — Making Events Accessible
sources.inspected_sections: Advance accessible material, captioning, visual description, processing time
sources.supported_use: Support usable formats and access to essential presentation information.
sources.limits: No claim that this source batch meets all accessibility standards. Learning-style wording is not adopted as a learning-style matching theory. Actual participant needs and access remain to be checked.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare — Giving and Receiving Feedback Activity, Christine Kelly course (2008)
sources.inspected_sections: Language of feedback; observation/evaluation; recipient clarity on evidence, impact and request
sources.supported_use: Feedback can be anchored to observed behavior and an understandable request.
sources.limits: An educational activity, not an effectiveness trial. No public personal-disclosure exercise or mandatory script reproduced; invitation and revise/retest design are original.

sources.title: Aristotle — Rhetoric, Book I, W. Rhys Roberts translation
sources.inspected_sections: Part 2: modes of persuasion; Part 3: speaker, subject and audience
sources.supported_use: Classical distinction among speaker credibility, audience emotion and apparent proof/reasoning.
sources.limits: Historical analysis, not empirical validation or endorsement of all ancient practices/values. Modern ethical restrictions and cases are author design judgments.

sources.title: Dahlstrom (2014), Using narratives and storytelling to communicate science with nonexpert audiences
sources.inspected_sections: Abstract on narrative communication and ethical implications
sources.supported_use: Narrative can be engaging and persuasive, raising ethical questions.
sources.limits: Only abstract inspected; PMC challenge and PNAS route failed. No quantitative effect, universal superiority or detailed causal theory attributed to uninspected full text. Original cases distinguish story mechanism from evidence of prevalence.

sources.title: MIT NSE Communication Lab — Delivery and Q&A
sources.inspected_sections: Practice, transitions, timing, audience practice and questions
sources.supported_use: Use actual rehearsal to edit a talk and find unclear transitions.
sources.limits: Technical-presentation guidance, not controlled outcome evidence. Eye-contact or standing norms are not imported as competence requirements; source examples and images are not copied.

sources.title: Harvard HMS/HSDM/HSPH Ombuds — Seven Elements of Effective Negotiations, Jerome Slavik (2008)
sources.kind: first-party institutional teaching handout adapting Getting to Yes
sources.inspected_sections: Interests, options, alternatives, legitimacy and commitments
sources.supported_use: Separate substantive interests, feasible alternatives, fair criteria and implementation.
sources.limits: The handout includes a suggestion to worsen the other side's alternative; this is explicitly excluded. No legal/financial advice, dependency exploitation or promise of mutual gain.

sources.title: Harvard PON — BATNA Analysis Can Help You Avoid the Agreement Trap (2025)
sources.inspected_sections: Agreement trap and comparing the deal with the alternative
sources.supported_use: Agreement alone is not a sufficient success criterion.
sources.limits: The page discusses research by others; this companion uses its institutional practice guidance, not an independently verified effect estimate or a claim that teams always negotiate better.

sources.title: Acas — Challenging conversations and how to manage them (July 2014)
sources.inspected_sections: Preparation, issue-specific evidence, listening and dated follow-up steps
sources.supported_use: Prepare specific issues and define a reviewable next step.
sources.limits: UK workplace/manager context and dated legal material are not transplanted into universal advice. No managerial power, coercive questioning, health disclosure or duty to confront is imported. Peer case and safe-ending boundaries are original.

sources.title: Kant and Norman (2019), You Must Be Joking!
sources.supported_use: Speaker/listener perspectives and power/culture can differ in humor judgments.
sources.limits: Conceptual analysis, not a validated diagnostic checklist or prediction model. No assumption about an individual from a group label. Target/timing/cost and repair tasks are original applications.
